name: Sony WF-1000XM5 Wireless Earbuds
verdict: The best wireless earbuds overall — class-leading sound, elite noise cancellation, and Sony's deep feature set.
description: The Sony WF-1000XM5 are the earbuds audiophiles and reviewers keep coming back to. The Dynamic Driver X delivers deep, textured bass alongside clear mids and highs, and the Integrated Processor V2 drives noise cancellation that rivals over-ear headphones. Battery life reaches about 8 hours with ANC on (24 with the case), and the companion app offers a graphic EQ, LDAC high-res streaming, and adaptive sound control. They're premium-priced, but for pure sound and ANC they set the bar.
features: Dynamic Driver X for detailed, full-range sound
Integrated Processor V2 with excellent ANC
~8hr battery (24hr with case) with ANC on
Adaptive Sound Control and graphic EQ in app
pros: Smaller, lighter design than the XM4
cons: Ear tips are foam and wear over time
No aptX support for some Android setups

name: Apple AirPods Pro (2nd Generation, USB-C)
verdict: The best earbuds for iPhone users — the deepest Apple ecosystem integration plus big ANC and hearing-health features.
description: The AirPods Pro (2nd generation) with USB-C are the default pick for iPhone owners. The H2 chip powers noise cancellation that's dramatically improved over the original Pro, Adaptive Audio that blends ANC and transparency based on your surroundings, and a clinical-grade Hearing Aid feature added via software. Spatial audio with head tracking creates an immersive experience, and conversation awareness lowers volume when you start talking. For anyone in the Apple ecosystem, nothing integrates as seamlessly.
features: Apple H2 chip with much-improved ANC
Adaptive Audio blends ANC and transparency
Spatial audio with dynamic head tracking
USB-C charging case with speaker and lanyard loop
cons: No high-res or aptX codec support
Ear tips only fit so many ear shapes

name: Bose QuietComfort Ultra Earbuds
verdict: The best noise-canceling earbuds — Bose's ANC is still the gold standard for silencing your surroundings.
description: When pure noise cancellation is the priority, Bose still wears the crown. The QuietComfort Ultra Earbuds block more ambient noise than almost any competitor — subway rumble, airplane engines, and office chatter largely disappear. Bose Immersive Audio adds spatial depth to music and podcasts, and CustomTune automatically calibrates the sound and ANC to the shape of your ear. Aware mode with ActiveSense lets voices through while still blocking background noise, making them excellent for travel and the office.
features: Bose Immersive Audio for spatial sound
pros: Immersive Audio adds real spatial depth
cons: Sound trails Sony for some listeners

name: Samsung Galaxy Buds 3 Pro
verdict: The best earbuds for Samsung users — seamless Galaxy integration, strong ANC, and excellent call quality.
description: If you live in the Samsung ecosystem, the Galaxy Buds 3 Pro are the obvious choice. They auto-switch between your Galaxy phone, tablet, and laptop, and the Galaxy Wearable app offers deep customization including a detailed EQ, 360 Audio with head tracking, and adjustable ANC. The redesigned blade-style stem and new fit improve comfort and call pickup, and the dual-driver setup delivers clean, balanced sound. The SSC Hi-Fi codec enables near-studio-quality streaming from Samsung devices.
features: SSC Hi-Fi codec for Samsung devices
Detailed EQ in Galaxy Wearable app
cons: Full features require a Samsung Galaxy device
Stems protrude more than some rivals

name: Google Pixel Buds Pro 2
verdict: The best earbuds for Pixel and Android users — Gemini AI, a superb comfortable fit, and Google's clean software.
description: Google's Pixel Buds Pro 2 are among the most comfortable earbuds you can buy — a smaller, lighter design with a twist-to-adjust fit that stays put during workouts without ear fatigue on long listens. The Tensor A1 chip powers effective noise cancellation and on-device processing, and Gemini integration lets you ask questions, get translations, and control your phone hands-free. Sound is balanced and natural, and Find My Device integration means you'll rarely lose them.
features: Tensor A1 chip for ANC and on-device processing
pros: Among the most comfortable earbuds available
Improved ANC over the first generation
cons: ANC still trails Bose and Sony slightly
Best features need an Android/Pixel device

name: Beats Fit Pro Wireless Earbuds
verdict: The best earbuds for workouts — a secure wingtip design that works great with both iPhone and Android.
description: The Beats Fit Pro solve the biggest problem with workout earbuds: they stay put. The flexible wingtip locks into your ear and won't budge during running, jumping, or lifting. Powered by Apple's H1 chip, they get active noise cancellation, transparency mode, and spatial audio on both iOS and Android (most Apple-chip earbuds limit Android features). Sound is punchy and bass-forward — ideal for workout playlists — and a quick charge gives an hour of playback in five minutes.
features: Apple H1 chip — works with iPhone AND Android
Spatial audio with dynamic head tracking
pros: Full features on both iOS and Android

name: Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 Open-Ear Headphones
verdict: The best open-ear option — hear your surroundings while running or cycling, with better bass than any Shokz before.
description: The Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 rest on your cheekbones and leave your ear canals completely open, so you hear traffic, conversations, and your surroundings while listening. For runners, cyclists, and outdoor exercisers, that awareness is a safety feature no in-ear bud can match. The new DualPitch design adds a small air-conduction driver for genuinely improved bass over past Shokz models. With 12 hours of battery, IP55 resistance, and a durable, flexible frame, they're built for serious training.
pros: All-day comfort with glasses and hats
cons: Open design can't match in-ear isolation

name: Nothing Ear (a) Wireless Earbuds
verdict: The best style-and-value pick — striking transparent design, strong ANC, and big battery life under $100.
description: The Nothing Ear (a) pair a distinctive transparent design with performance that punches above their price. The 11mm driver delivers lively, customizable sound, hybrid ANC rated up to 45dB silences commuter noise, and LDAC support brings high-res streaming to Android. Battery life is excellent at up to 9.5 hours per charge (42.5 with the case), and the app offers a detailed EQ plus a Bass Enhance feature. For design-conscious buyers who don't want to spend flagship money, they're hard to beat.
features: Up to 9.5hr per charge (42.5hr with case)
pros: LDAC support is rare this cheap
cons: Call quality is average in wind
Case is larger than some rivals

name: EarFun Air Pro 4 Wireless Earbuds
verdict: The best budget ANC earbuds — flagship features like aptX Lossless and LDAC at a fraction of the price.
description: The EarFun Air Pro 4 prove you don't need to spend $250 for an excellent set of noise-canceling earbuds. They deliver adaptive hybrid ANC that genuinely quiets commuter noise, Qualcomm Snapdragon Sound with aptX Lossless and LDAC for high-res audio, and a warm, detailed signature that punches well above the price. Battery life is strong at up to 11 hours per charge (52 with the case), and the app offers a full EQ, ANC adjustment, and low-latency game mode. For non-audiophiles, these may be all the earbuds you ever need.
features: aptX Lossless and LDAC high-res codecs
pros: Wireless charging is rare this cheap
cons: ANC isn't as strong as Sony or Bose
Call quality is good, not great
Fit can be shallow for some ears

name: Anker Soundcore Liberty 4 NC
verdict: The cheapest earbuds with genuinely good ANC — adaptive noise cancellation and 50-hour battery around $100.
description: The Soundcore Liberty 4 NC are among the most affordable noise-canceling earbuds worth recommending. Adaptive ANC adjusts to your environment in real time, and the 98.5% noise reduction claim holds up well against commuter noise and office chatter. Sound is warm and bass-forward — great for pop and hip-hop — and LDAC support adds high-res streaming on Android. Battery life is excellent at up to 10 hours per charge (50 total), and the Soundcore app includes a full EQ plus a HearID test that personalizes sound to your hearing.
pros: HearID personalization is a nice touch
cons: Fit test matters to get the seal right
